The portrait scene's adult-nest association, maternity, attendance, guarding implication, egg appearance, egg count, and exact moment.
The familiar Korean framing '착한 엄마 공룡' is a child-facing cultural label, not direct proof of feeding or maternal attendance.

prompt: Use case: scientific-educational
Asset type: Dino Atlas gallery representative image for Korean children ages 5-14

Primary request: Create a new original, copyright-safe naturalistic paleoart reconstruction of one adult Maiasaura peeblesorum. This must be a strict full-body identity image, not based on or imitating any named artist or existing artwork.

Scene/backdrop: Late Cretaceous Campanian Two Medicine Formation upland floodplain in Montana, a shallow dry braided wash with weathered volcanic-ash-rich sediment, sparse conifers, ferns, horsetails, and low flowering shrubs. No modern grass lawn.

Subject: exactly ONE adult Maiasaura peeblesorum. A large saurolophine hadrosaur with a moderately elongated face, broad closed toothless duck bill, and the diagnostic short solid transverse crest rising vertically above the skull roof between the eyes. The crest is compact and low, never a long tube, backward spike, tall helmet, or fan. Thick neck, deep barrel-shaped hadrosaur torso, robust hind limbs, shorter weight-bearing forelimbs, compact padded mitten-like forehands, three broad main toes on each hind foot, and one long stiff tail held clear of the ground. Exactly two forelimbs, exactly two hind limbs, two separate forehands, two separate hind feet, one head, and one continuous tail.
Style/medium: polished museum-quality natural-history illustration, anatomically conservative, realistic skin and weight, child-friendly and non-cartoon, no dramatic monster styling.

Composition/framing: landscape. Low eye-level lateral three-quarter view, walking calmly left-to-right across the wash. Show the complete animal from bill to tail tip with generous empty margin. Stagger all four limbs so every limb and foot connection is readable; no limb overlap with the body, vegetation, rocks, or shadows. Keep the head, crest, hands, feet, pelvis, and tail base sharply readable at thumbnail scale.
Lighting/mood: clear neutral morning light, calm observational mood, no heavy fog, dust cloud, motion blur, or extreme rim light.

Color palette: smoky indigo-gray dorsum and limbs, muted mulberry side field, warm apricot shoulder patch, pale flax underside. Irregular soft-edged flank dapples only; no regular tail rings. Matte pebbled skin, restrained keratin on bill and nails.

Constraints: no text, labels, borders, infographic, split panel, logo, watermark, signature, blood, wounds, nest, eggs, juveniles, herd, predator, active eruption, falling ash, fantasy anatomy, or named-artist imitation.

Avoid: Parasaurolophus tubular crest, Saurolophus backward spike, Corythosaurus helmet, Lambeosaurus hatchet crest, Edmontosaurus crestless head, Iguanodon thumb spike, Triceratops frill or horns, theropod teeth, visible separated clawed fingers, elephant feet, rhinoceros proportions, lizard sprawl, modern bird plumage, dorsal sail, dorsal spikes, extra or fused limbs, missing feet, duplicated toes, cropped or forked tail.
